mutants.expected_detection: Harness calls kernel_access with op=READ and negative indices (e.g., -1, -1000, INT_MIN) on a scratchpad pre-filled with sentinel values. The mutated bounds check only rejects index >= BUFFER_SIZE, so negative indices pass validation and scratchpad[index] is read out-of-bounds (into adjacent memory before the buffer), violating status/return-value expectations and potentially crashing or leaking adjacent memory contents, which SR1's memcmp/status/return checks will detect.

Harness calls kernel_access with op=WRITE and index == BUFFER_SIZE (64), which should be rejected per SR2/FR3 (index must be strictly < BUFFER_SIZE). With the off-by-one bound, the check index > BUFFER_SIZE lets index==64 pass validation, causing scratchpad[64] = write_val to write one int32_t past the end of the buffer into adjacent (canary) memory. memcmp of the canary region will show corruption, and status will incorrectly be 0 instead of 1.

Harness probes extreme int32 values (e.g. INT_MIN, INT_MAX, and values like 65536+5) and finds that truncating index to a 16-bit value before bounds-checking allows out-of-range indices whose low 16 bits fall within [0,BUFFER_SIZE) to bypass validation, causing an out-of-bounds read/write on the underlying scratchpad array.

Harness calls kernel_access with op values other than 0/1 (e.g., 2, -1, 999) on valid in-range indices; the mutant treats any unrecognized op as an implicit WRITE, so scratchpad is modified and the write_val is returned with status=0 instead of status=1/return 0/no modification, causing SR4 behavioral checks to fail.

Harness performs an in-range WRITE at index i with write_val, then reads back scratchpad[i] or checks the returned value; because the write stores write_val+1 instead of write_val, the returned value and stored buffer contents mismatch the expected write_val, failing the in-range functional/side-effect check (SR5).

In-range READ test vectors (e.g., index=0) will fail: kernel_access returns scratchpad[index+1] instead of scratchpad[index], producing a wrong value for FR1-covered functional test vectors, and can also read out of bounds when index==BUFFER_SIZE-1.

SR5/FR2 functional test vector: in-range WRITE at a valid index expects scratchpad[index] to be updated to write_val and the same value returned with status=0; this mutant removes the actual store to scratchpad[index] so the buffer retains its old value while still returning write_val and status=0, causing a mismatch when the harness reads back the written index or memcmp's the buffer against expected post-write state.

SR1/SR2/FR3 behavioral tests: harness calls kernel_access with an out-of-range index (e.g. index == BUFFER_SIZE, or negative) and asserts status==1 and return value==0. With this mutant, out-of-range accesses report *status = STATUS_SUCCESS (stuck at 0) instead of STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RANGE, so the status output is always 0 regardless of range validity, causing the out-of-range test vectors to fail on the status field even though the array itself is not touched.

Harness compiles against BUFFER_SIZE=64 contract; with BUFFER_SIZE redefined to 32 in the kernel file, in-range functional test vectors using indices 32-63 (valid under the required BUFFER_SIZE=64 interface) will be incorrectly rejected as out-of-range (status=1, return 0) instead of performing the expected read/write, causing FR1/FR2/FR4 behavioral checks to fail and revealing the interface/capacity contract violation.
